svg.title: Which library changes break downstream code
svg.desc: Changes that are major, meaning breaking: removing or renaming a public item, adding a variant to an exhaustive enum, adding a public field to a struct without non_exhaustive, adding a trait method without a default, adding a bound to a generic, changing a function signature. Changes that are minor: adding a new public item, adding a variant to a non_exhaustive enum, adding a trait method with a default (with a caveat about name collisions), adding a method to a sealed trait, relaxing a bound. cargo-semver-checks catches many of these automatically.
svg.text: Is this change a major or a minor version bump?
For a 1.x crate. Under 0.x, Cargo treats 0.y as the major version.
Major: breaks some caller
Remove or rename a pub item
Add a variant to an exhaustive enum
Add a pub field to an exhaustive struct
Add a trait method with no default
Add a bound to a generic parameter
Change a pub fn signature
Stop implementing Send, Sync, or a trait
Minor: callers keep compiling
Add a new pub fn, type or module
Add a variant to a #[non_exhaustive] enum
Add a field to a #[non_exhaustive] struct
Add any method to a sealed trait
Add a defaulted trait method *
Relax a bound on a generic
Implement a new trait for a type *
* minor, but can cause method-name clashes
cargo semver-checks
compares your public API to the last release and flags many of these
